claim: On an 8-card CMP 170HX box at PCIe Gen2 x4 with no P2P, tensor parallelism is not an option and pipeline parallelism is the only viable topology: the repo states 'TP is not an option on this box (no P2P); PP6 saves only ~6%.'
stance_target: the repo's claim that tensor parallelism is ruled out by the fabric, on the exact Gen2 x4 no-P2P configuration the query names
scope_conditions: 8x CMP 170HX (GA100, SM80, 64 GB unlocked), PCIe Gen2 x4 each, no P2P, 2x Xeon E5-2690 v4 host, 96 GB DDR4; GLM-5.3-Flash 320B MoE / 18B active / 1M context, NVFP4 weights, DFlash2 drafter; community-reported, single author, one commit
quoted_support: TP is not an option on this box (no P2P); PP6 saves only ~6%.

claim: A 960,000-token prompt completes end-to-end in 208 s on 8 cards at Gen2 x4 with the needle retrieved, and a 192,000-token prompt in 53 s — implying roughly 4,600 tok/s aggregate prefill across eight cards at the 1M scale.
stance_target: the feasibility of a 1M-token global batch on this fabric: a single 1M-token forward pass costs ~208 s of prefill on 8 cards, so a training step at 1M tokens is on the order of minutes even before backward
scope_conditions: 8x CMP 170HX at Gen2 x4, no P2P, GLM-5.3-Flash NVFP4 PP8 + DFlash2 k=7, --max-model-len 1048576, --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90, KV pool 6.62M tokens
quoted_support: Long context (`scripts/needle.py`, prod config): 192k-token prompt in 53 s, **960k-token prompt in 208 s** end-to-end, needle retrieved; KV pool 6.62M tokens (6.3 concurrent 1M requests) at utilization 0.90.

claim: The measured PP8 step-time model on this Gen2 x4 box is ~32 ms fixed plus 2.1 ms per verified token, where the fixed part is the serial 8-stage pipeline (attention/KDA/dense per stage plus hops plus host prep/sampling) and the variable part is active-expert weight bandwidth scaling with tokens x top-k.
stance_target: the cost-model shape for pipeline parallelism on a Gen2 x4 fabric, which is what makes PP viable where TP is not
scope_conditions: 8x CMP 170HX at Gen2 x4, measured with per-stage CUDA events (patches 0018/0019)
quoted_support: Step time model measured with per-stage CUDA events (patch 0018/0019): `≈ 32 ms fixed + 2.1 ms × verified tokens per step`. The fixed part is the 8-stage serial pipeline (attention/KDA/dense per stage + hops + host prep/sampling); the variable part is active-expert weight bandwidth (bytes ∝ tokens × top-k).

claim: Speculative decoding is worth roughly 20x on this stack: FP8 eager with no speculation decoded code at 6.2 tok/s, while NVFP4 + DFlash2 k=7 reached 123 tok/s on code, 120 on json, 114-118 on counting, 59 on math and 37 on prose.
stance_target: how much of the achievable throughput on this box comes from engine and drafter work rather than hardware — relevant to sizing any training-throughput estimate
scope_conditions: 8x CMP 170HX at Gen2 x4, single stream, temperature 0, tokens/s including speculative decoding, scripts/bench.py

claim: Steady-state aggregate throughput at 1M-capable context scales from 201-203 tok/s at 4 streams to 259-267 at 8 and 276 at 16.
stance_target: the aggregate throughput envelope of an 8-card Gen2 x4 box, which bounds what a training run could expect from the same fabric
scope_conditions: 8x CMP 170HX at Gen2 x4, chat workload, 200-token completions, scripts/conc2.py

claim: The layer partition is chosen around the 11 sparse-MLA layers (indices 3, 7, ..., 43) so that stages holding two of them get fewer layers and a larger KV budget, yielding VLLM_PP_LAYER_PARTITION=7,5,7,5,7,5,7,2 for an 8-stage run.
stance_target: the memory-balance problem any pipeline-parallel training run would inherit: layer count per stage is dictated by KV and weight footprint, not by an even split
quoted_support: Layer partition is chosen around the 11 sparse-MLA layers (idx 3,7,…,43): stages holding two of them get fewer layers so their KV budget is larger.

claim: The patch set is 24 commits on top of the official vLLM image (65 files, +4.8k/-0.2k), and the single highest-impact fix is loading the MTP draft model's embed_tokens and shared_head.head weights from the checkpoint under pipeline parallelism, which upstream skips and leaves randomly initialized, driving acceptance to zero.
stance_target: the engineering cost of making PP work on this stack — PP is viable but requires a substantial patch set, not a configuration change
scope_conditions: vllm/vllm-openai:glm53-flash (v0.1.dev20051+g487ecf187) + patches/, Apache-2.0 derivative of vLLM
quoted_support: `patches/NNNN-*.patch` are the 24 commits on top of the image's `vllm/` package, in order; `patches/all-changes-vs-baseline.diff` is the same as one diff (65 files, +4.8k/-0.2k). ... 3. MTP under PP: draft `embed_tokens` / `shared_head.head` loaded from the checkpoint (target→draft sharing is skipped under PP upstream, leaving them random → 0% acceptance)
